basis: The Commission credits the agreements signed or in force with its progress statements on coordination and repeats its recommendation to conclude more with Member States from 2023 to 2026.
The Commission reports the negotiations with other Member States in direct answer to its recommendation to conclude additional agreements.
The National Accession Programme lists the decree on initiating negotiations as an action on social security agreements with Member States.
The National Accession Programme lists the administrative arrangement for applying the agreements as an action on social security coordination.
The 2024 report presents the proposed upgrade of the Italy agreement under its recommendation on agreements with Member States.
The Commission reports the agreement with Spain under social security coordination with Member States.
The Commission reports the agreement with Greece under social security coordination with Member States.
The Commission reports the agreement with Latvia under social security coordination with Member States.
The Commission reports the agreement with Italy under social security coordination with Member States.
The Commission reports the agreement with France under social security coordination with Member States.
The 2026 report names the Slovakia agreement as the basis for good progress on agreements with Member States.
The 2024 report presents the action plan on joining EURES as the response to its recommendation to start preparatory work.
The 2026 report names the designation of the National Employment Agency as National Coordination Office as preparation for joining EURES.
The Commission states that the September 2025 Decision establishes the national legal framework for EURES activities.
The Government states that the 2024 Decision ensures partial alignment with the EURES Regulation.
The order sets the procedure for admission as EURES member or partner, which the Commission records as preparation for joining EURES.
The 2026 report records the implementing acts on EURES data collection and monitoring as part of preparation to join the network.
The National Accession Programme lists the draft agency orders as EURES implementing measures.
Interoperability of the agency's system with the EURES platform is one of the steps the Government names as needed to complete accession to EURES.
The Government links the ESCO correlation tables to automated matching through the EURES common IT platform.
The draft law extends the agency's competences to carry out its tasks as EURES National Coordination Office.
The feasibility study concerns the introduction of the European Health Insurance Card, as the Commission reports in 2026.
The Government's commitment to apply the Card is stated alongside its finding that the EU acts on the Card are not transposed.
The draft law on cross-border medical care in Member States is listed with the Card measures in the National Accession Programme.
The Commission reports the accessibility law in the same 2026 report that recommends improving digital accessibility; it covers products and services, including digital services.
The order sets WCAG 2.2 accessibility rules for public websites, the subject of the 2026 recommendation.
SIGMA reports the website guidelines and the planned unified interface for government websites in its finding on poor accessibility compliance.
The Reform Agenda states that Moldova will adapt its framework to comply with the EU 5G Cybersecurity Toolbox.
The Government states the study analyses the impact and risks of implementing the EU 5G Toolbox.
The contract provides a 5G vendor risk assessment and a draft law aligning with the EU 5G Toolbox.
The Government presents the draft law on 5G network cybersecurity as its action on the EU 5G Toolbox.
The draft Decision on 5G network cybersecurity applies Commission Recommendation (EU) 2019/534 underlying the Toolbox.
The 2026 report records secondary legislation on security of public 5G networks under the cybersecurity framework.
The Commission recommended finalising the NCTS and records its rollout as progress in customs IT.
The Commission recommended finalising preparations to join the Common Transit Convention, and records the accession in 2026.
The 2024 report asks Moldova to approve and implement this IT strategy for interoperability with the EU electronic customs environment.
The Commission states the programme prioritises interconnectivity and interoperability with EU customs systems, as its 2025 recommendation asked.
The 2025 recommendation asks for the Customs Decisions System with all 17 applications operational, and the 2026 report records it aligned with the EU Customs Data Model.
The Commission states the Decision establishes the national Customs Decisions System as the future national component of the EU system.
The 2026 report states the Customs Code amendments will provide the legal basis for full automation and EU-interoperable systems.
The 2025 report names ICS2 among the technical arrangements still pending for the Common Transit Convention.
The EU states the expert assistance prepares the ground for interoperability with the EU electronic customs environment.
The Government plans the AI law to transpose the EU AI Act, which the Commission found Moldova not yet aligned with.
The Government plans to designate or establish an AI governance institution, matching the Commission's call for governance and enforcement structures.
The programme states harmonisation with the AI Act as a critical dimension and plans a national regulatory framework on AI.
The draft law establishes regulated AI testing spaces, an element of the AI regulatory framework.
The Government states that implementing the AI acquis requires the new consultant post.
The Commission reports the sub-council on AI and data as Moldova's step on AI governance.
The Government describes the White Paper as its first policy framework towards an AI regulatory framework aligned with the EU.
The Commission assesses the law's alignment with the EU eIDAS Regulation.
The Government presents Law No. 117/2025 as updating Law No. 124/2022 in line with EU trust services rules.
The Commission states the December 2025 amendments fully aligned Moldova with EU requirements for qualified trust service providers.
The draft law transposes the European Digital Identity Regulation (eIDAS 2), which the Commission and Reform Agenda require.
The draft orders implement the European Digital Identity framework and trust services under eIDAS 2.
The draft Decision sets electronic identification assurance levels under the eIDAS framework.
The Commission asks for interoperability with the European Digital Identity Wallets, and the Government plans the wallet in line with Regulation (EU) 2024/1183.
The Commission reports the national strategy to align with eIDAS 2.0, including the wallet amendments.
The Commission and Government present the Law on cybersecurity as aligning with the NIS framework.
The Commission states the implementing Government Decisions aim to ensure alignment with NIS 2.
The draft law amends Law No. 48/2023 to transpose NIS 2, which the Reform Agenda sets out.
The Commission records the programme as setting national cyber resilience objectives after the earlier strategy lapsed.
The Government states the Decision, with Law No. 48/2023, transposes NIS 2 obligations for service providers in critical sectors.
The Decision regulates state supervision of compliance with the cybersecurity framework under Law No. 48/2023.
The Reform Agenda and Government present the draft law as alignment with the Cyber Resilience Act.
The Government lists the certification scheme law as transposition of the EU acquis on cybersecurity certification.
The Government lists designating the market surveillance authority as part of transposing the Cyber Resilience Act.
The Government and the Interoperable Europe factsheet present the Council as coordinating cybersecurity policy under the cybersecurity law.
The Commission asks for operational capacity of the Cybersecurity Agency and reports its strengthening in 2025 and 2026.
The national CERT is the incident response capacity whose operationalisation the Commission tracks from 2021 to 2026.
The Decision establishes the Cybersecurity Agency as the competent authority, as the cybersecurity law required.
The Government presents the register as a system for recording and managing cyber incidents at the Agency.
The Government lists cybersecurity training for civil servants and technical staff under strengthening operational capacity.
The Agency reports the exercises as testing technical skills and response to cyber incidents.
The Commission states the CERT became fully operational after approval of the Directorate's rules of procedure.
The Commission reports the EU donation of equipment and licences for the Agency under the Reform Agenda step on operational capacity.
The Commission reports EUPM software and seconded experts as support to the CERT team's operations.
The Commission reports TAIEX training for Agency departments, including the CERT team.
The EU states the crisis response measure was adopted to strengthen Moldova's cybersecurity.
The 2026 report states that the NCTS Phase 6 rollout facilitated full accession to the Common Transit Convention and enhanced the interoperability of customs operations.
The Government states that the agreements allow better social protection for Moldovan citizens working abroad.
The Government states that progress in building a resilient cyber ecosystem was accelerated by the EU Cybersecurity Rapid Assistance Project.
